**Transportation Model**

Let  

- \(I\) be the set of Walmart stores (indexed by \(i\)).  
- \(J\) be the set of customer groups (indexed by \(j\)).  

Parameters  

- \(s_i\) : daily supply capacity of store \(i\)  \((i \in I)\).  
- \(d_j\) : daily demand of customer group \(j\)  \((j \in J)\).  
- \(c_{ij}\) : transportation cost per unit from store \(i\) to customer group \(j\)  \((i \in I,\; j \in J)\).  

Decision variables  

- \(x_{ij} \ge 0\) : quantity transported from store \(i\) to customer group \(j\)  \((i \in I,\; j \in J)\).  

**Model**

\[
\begin{aligned}
\min \quad & \sum_{i \in I}\sum_{j \in J} c_{ij}\,x_{ij} \\[6pt]
\text{s.t.}\quad
& \sum_{j \in J} x_{ij} \;\le\; s_i, && \forall i \in I \quad \text{(supply capacity)}\\[4pt]
& \sum_{i \in I} x_{ij} \;=\; d_j, && \forall j \in J \quad \text{(demand satisfaction)}\\[4pt]
& x_{ij} \;\ge\; 0, && \forall i \in I,\; j \in J
\end{aligned}
\]

This linear programming formulation minimizes total transportation cost while ensuring that each store’s supply limit is not exceeded and every customer group’s demand is met exactly.

from gurobipy import GRB

dem = [/* demand per product */]

m = gp.Model("Product_Sales")

x = m.addVars(len(rev), vtype=GRB.INTEGER, name="x")

# Objective function
